Question B-005-008-006.

Why the correct answer is right: A decibel expresses a ratio between two signal levels. It is useful for gain and loss because doubled, halved, ten-times, and one-tenth changes become decibels (dB) changes.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "To describe a waveform on an oscilloscope": An oscilloscope display can show shape and timing, but decibel is not the waveform-shape name.
- sourceIndex 2: "To describe very high frequency radio waves": Very-high-frequency (VHF) identifies a frequency range. Decibels compare levels, not bands.
- sourceIndex 3: "To measure a single side band signal": A decibel does not identify the single sideband (SSB) mode itself; it compares one signal or power level with another.
